gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-012 concerns unsupported joint data-and-dictionary eigenpair convergence caused by boundedness and limiting-argument gaps. It does not identify the separate introductory overstatement that spectral convergence is general rather than conditional on subsequences and a nonzero weak limit.

ISSUE-010 discusses identification and boundedness of a finite-dimensional empirical operator under data-limit hypotheses. It does not recognize the distinct well-definedness failure of composition on L-infinity equivalence classes or the missing nonsingularity condition.

ISSUE-010 concerns boundedness and identification of the data-limit empirical operator, not the sampled-value quotient sending an empirical zero representative to a nonzero operator value. It supplies no diagnosis of the sampling non-injectivity and resulting failure of well-definedness.

ISSUE-006 identifies an eta-versus-xi formula mismatch in the noisy estimator and its Bernstein proof. It does not recognize the separate covariance bias in E[gg†] and E[cg†], nor the resulting nonvanishing asymptotic bias and need for covariance correction or replicate data.

Both identify that conditioning on all M independent truncation events gives probability p̃_N^M, so multiplying by only p̃_N does not establish the claimed unconditional confidence. Both specify the corresponding p̃_N^M correction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The noisy confidence conversion uses the single-sample probability instead of the probability of the joint M-sample truncation event, invalidating the unconditional guarantee and its dependent theorem.

component_coverage.gold_component: The conditioning event intersects the truncation events for all M samples and therefore has probability p̃_N^M, not p̃_N.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the all-sample conditioning event, derives probability (p̃_N)^M, and identifies the false change-of-measure inequality.

component_coverage.gold_component: The incorrect calibration lowers the unconditional confidence and requires replacing the multiplier and dependent theorem conditions by the M-sample calibration.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the failure of the claimed unconditional probability and gives the specific corrected (p̃_N)^M change-of-measure relation and repair alternatives.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-011 raises separate uniform spectral-bound and adjoint-domain problems in the Galerkin eigenpair argument. It does not identify the invalid inference from fixed-vector projection convergence to norm convergence of (I-P_N)Af_N, nor the valid pairing-based repair.
